claims.text: Wear performance in FeNiCrCoCu HEA coatings is governed by temperature-induced changes in lattice disorder and dislocation density.
Up to 600 K, the coating retains an ordered FCC lattice.
Up to 600 K, the coating retains a stable dislocation network.
Retention of the ordered FCC lattice and stable dislocation network supports good wear resistance up to 600 K.
Above approximately 900 K, rapid lattice softening occurs.
Above approximately 900 K, the fraction of atoms classified as HCP increases.
Above approximately 900 K, dislocation density decreases significantly.
High temperature shifts deformation from stacking-fault-mediated plasticity to deformation dominated by lattice disorder.
The high-temperature structural changes cause a sharp decrease in hardness.
The high-temperature structural changes cause a sharp decrease in elastic modulus.
The high-temperature structural changes increase the friction coefficient relative to the 300 K baseline.
The high-temperature structural changes increase tangential force relative to the 300 K baseline.
The modeled initial state is a 21 Å FeNiCrCoCu coating adhered to a single-crystal Cu matrix measuring 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å.
The coating and Cu matrix are initialized as FCC structures with [100], [010], and [001] orientations.
The controlled intervention compares simulations at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K using a 300 K baseline.
The virtual indenter is pressed at 10 m/s to a depth of 30 Å, with 300 ps loading and 300 ps unloading.
Approximately 900 K is the critical temperature threshold for rapid structural disorder and mechanical degradation.
